title: TrustBundleStore is keyed by TrustDomain::to_string and panics on a poisoned lock
description:
persona-core/src/trust_bundle.rs:36-71.

Key type leak: `upsert()` derives the map key internally with `bundle.trust_domain.to_string()` (trust_bundle.rs:47) but `get()` takes `&str` (trust_bundle.rs:65). A caller must reproduce the `Display` impl of `TrustDomain` (spiffe_id.rs:51-62) exactly to look anything up — including knowing that `PersonalDid(x)` is keyed `personal.{x}` and `PivIssuer(x)` is keyed `piv.{x}`. There is no public parse in the other direction (see the TrustDomain injectivity issue), so the map is effectively write-only for external callers unless they hand-format keys. `get()` should take `&TrustDomain`.

Undocumented panics: all three public methods `unwrap` the RwLock with `.expect("trust bundle lock poisoned")` (trust_bundle.rs:50, 57, 68). Nothing in the doc comments mentions this. The store is explicitly designed for concurrent use ("Thread-safe store", trust_bundle.rs:31) and is shared as `Arc<TrustBundleStore>` across gRPC handlers (persona-grpc/src/service.rs:18); one panic anywhere under the write lock turns every subsequent FetchJWTBundles/FetchX509Bundles call into a daemon panic rather than a Status error. Either document the panic on each method or hold the lock in a way that cannot poison (the guarded section does no user code, so `.unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())` is correct and removes the failure mode entirely).

Minor, same file: `TrustBundle` is `#[non_exhaustive]` (trust_bundle.rs:6) yet `new()` (trust_bundle.rs:18) takes all three fields positionally, so adding the fourth field that non_exhaustive was added to allow still breaks every caller. `TrustBundle.trust_domain` (trust_bundle.rs:9) and `TrustBundleStore::new` (trust_bundle.rs:41) have no doc comment, and the module has no `//!` header unlike every other module in the crate.
